ownership_reason: Only the gold looks at the kind of a child node and copies the data nodes into the result; hop 2 only wraps the list it gets back as an unmodifiable list, and hops 1, 3 and 4 pass the child node list along unchanged. The gold's javadoc promises the data nodes of a list of child nodes, in document order; a data node that is the last child (the script's only child) is a data node, yet the gold copies only the data nodes that are followed by a node that is not a data node. No one-line change above the gold recovers the left-out data nodes while keeping the gold's result (that is a filtering loop, i.e. the gold's own computation). The convention is pinned outside the gold: Element.textNodes keeps every TextNode child of the same childNodes list, the last one included; Element.data appends the data of every DataNode child (recursing into elements); Document.normaliseTextNodes filters every child node with an instanceof test; ElementTest testGetTextNodes (the third of p's text nodes is its last child ' Four') and HtmlParserTest handlesDataOnlyTags (a style whose only child is a data node has that node's data) pass; the facade's own javadoc calls dataNodes 'effectively a filter on childNodes() to get Data nodes'.
